Routing notes:
- Large east-region claim requests → C (regional office). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2404, 2405, 2407, and 2409.
- Large east-region invoice requests → do not use C; C was rejected for REQ-2400, 2402, 2403, and 2408. Route to either A (standard queue) or B (priority desk); evidence does not distinguish which.
- Large east-region refund requests → do not use C; C was rejected for REQ-2401 and 2406. Route to either A or B; evidence does not distinguish which.
- Sender, department, wording, and urgency cues shown did not establish a reliable alternative between A and B.

Routing notes:
- Large east-region claim requests → C (regional office). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2404, 2405, 2407, 2409, and 2413.
- Large east-region invoice requests → B (priority desk). C was rejected for REQ-2400, 2402, 2403, and 2408; A was rejected for REQ-2410, 2411, 2412, 2415, 2416, and 2419. Repeated evidence now supports B rather than the previous “A or B” uncertainty.
- Large east-region refund requests → A (standard queue). C was rejected for REQ-2401 and 2406; A was accepted for REQ-2414 and 2418.
- Sender, department, wording, urgency, and intake-format cues have not established a different routing rule.
- Large east-region shipment requests: A was rejected for REQ-2417. Do not assume the claim/invoice/refund rules apply; route only with further evidence.

Routing notes:
- Large east-region claim requests → C (regional office). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2404, 2405, 2407, 2409, 2413, and 2426.
- Large east-region invoice requests → B (priority desk). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2425, 2427, and 2429; prior rejections of A and C support B over the former “A or B” uncertainty.
- Large east-region refund requests → A (standard queue). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2420, 2423, and 2428, as well as REQ-2414 and 2418. C was rejected for REQ-2401 and 2406.
- Large east-region shipment requests → B (priority desk) is currently supported: B accepted for REQ-2424, while A was rejected for REQ-2417. Do not use claim/invoice/refund rules for shipments without further evidence. D is not a valid option (REQ-2421 and 2422).
- Sender, department, wording, urgency, and intake-format cues have not established a different routing rule.

Routing notes:
- Large east-region claim requests → C (regional office). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2404, 2405, 2407, 2409, 2413, 2426, and 2430.
- Large east-region invoice requests → B (priority desk). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2425, 2427, 2429, 2433–2435, and 2439. Prior rejections of A and C further rule out those alternatives.
- Large east-region refund requests → A (standard queue). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2414, 2418, 2420, 2423, 2428, and 2437. C was rejected for REQ-2401 and 2406.
- Large east-region shipment requests → B (priority desk). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2424 and 2431, 2432, 2436, and 2438; A was rejected for REQ-2417. Do not transfer claim/invoice/refund rules to shipments, though current shipment evidence consistently supports B. D is not valid (REQ-2421 and 2422).
- Sender, department, wording, urgency, and intake-format cues have not established a different routing rule. Recent examples include no-rush, urgent, bounced-form, and scanned-paperwork wording with the same request-type routing.

Routing notes:
- Large east-region claim requests → C (regional office). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2404, 2405, 2407, 2409, 2413, 2426, 2430, 2440, and 2447.
- Large east-region invoice requests → B (priority desk). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2425, 2427, 2429, 2433–2435, 2439, and 2442–2444. Rejections of A and C further rule out those alternatives.
- Large east-region refund requests → A (standard queue). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2414, 2418, 2420, 2423, 2428, 2437, and 2441, 2445, 2446, 2449. C was rejected for REQ-2401 and 2406.
- Large east-region shipment requests → B (priority desk). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2424, 2431–2432, 2436, 2438, and 2448; A was rejected for REQ-2417. D is invalid (REQ-2421–2422).
- Route by request type, not sender, department, wording, urgency, intake format, or stated submission path. Evidence includes no-rush, urgent, bounced-form, scanned-paperwork, repeated-follow-up, and “regional office” wording without changing the established routing.

Routing notes:
- Route large east-region requests by request type only; ignore sender, department, wording, urgency, intake format, and stated submission path.
- Claims → C (regional office). Confirmed: REQ-2404, 2405, 2407, 2409, 2413, 2426, 2430, 2440, 2447, 2450, 2458.
- Invoices → B (priority desk). Confirmed: REQ-2425, 2427, 2429, 2433–2435, 2439, 2442–2444, 2456. Rejections of A and C support this.
- Refunds → A (standard queue). Confirmed: REQ-2414, 2418, 2420, 2423, 2428, 2437, 2441, 2445, 2446, 2449, 2451–2453, 2455, 2459. C rejected for REQ-2401 and 2406.
- Shipments → B (priority desk). Confirmed: REQ-2424, 2431–2432, 2436, 2438, 2448, 2454, 2457. A rejected for REQ-2417; D invalid for REQ-2421–2422.
- Recent cases continue to show that follow-ups, scanned paperwork, “no rush,” end-of-day requests, and repeated/submission-related wording do not alter routing.
